youtube.title: Where was the first Formula 1 race? A bomber base and a king 🏁
youtube.description:
Monza, Monaco or the third one? The World Championship opened in May on a circuit laid out over the runways of a wartime bomber airfield, with a reigning king in the grandstand. The season had just seven rounds; this year's has 24.
Guess before the map lights up, then see the airfield, the first champion and the road to the finale.
Which did you pick?

research.topic: First Formula One World Championship race: British Grand Prix (Grand Prix d'Europe), Silverstone, 13 May 1950, on a circuit laid out on the runways and perimeter track of RAF Silverstone, a wartime Wellington bomber training base; attended by King George VI and Queen Elizabeth; won by Giuseppe Farina (Alfa Romeo 158), who clinched the first drivers' title at the Italian Grand Prix, Monza, 3 September 1950; the 1950 season had 7 rounds (incl. Indianapolis 500); the 2026 calendar has 24 rounds, finishing in Abu Dhabi in December.

myths.myth: Formula 1 began at Monza or Monaco, the sport's oldest famous circuits.
myths.reality: Monaco (1929) and Monza (1922) hosted Grands Prix long before the championship, but the first World Championship round was Silverstone on 13 May 1950.
